chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

There is no salat (prayer) except with taharah (ritual purity), and for istinja', three stones suffice you; by that the sunnah (prophetic tradition) from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was established. But as for urine, it must necessarily be washed.

key_terms.بِطَهُورٍ: with taharah (ritual purity), the required state for prayer
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَحْجَارٍ: three stones, the sufficient means of dry cleansing in this context
key_terms.صَلَاةَ: salat (prayer), whose validity depends on ritual purity
key_terms.غَسْلِهِ: washing it, indicating mandatory cleansing with water
key_terms.ٱلسُّنَّةُ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition), the normative practice traced to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about taharah (ritual purity), istinja', and washing urine before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that salat (prayer) is not valid without taharah (ritual purity). It also explains that in istinja', three stones are sufficient according to the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, while urine requires washing.
